entries.label: p3-r1 2026-11-19: 'in range — no rejection' + 'Findings: none' + 'will not be rejected'
entries.source: live leg p3-trace-r1 (adjudicated correct; old arms false-failed it)
entries.text:
**Command-level verdict: 240 is in range — no rejection.** I ran `PREHEAT T=240` through the simulator:

- **Rendered:** `M104 S240` → `M109 S240`
- **Findings: none** — every rendered command matched the registry shape on this invocation
- **Execution trace:** extruder target set to 240°C on both lines; final state `targets: extruder 240°C`. No refused line, no out-of-range rejection.

On the "does Klipper range-check S=" question specifically:

- The G-Codes reference documents these as `M104 [T<index>] [S<temperature>]` and `M109 [T<index>] S<temperature>` with **no range specified for S** — and the simulation confirms 240 passes cleanly.
- The only temperature ranges in the docs are `min_temp` / `max_temp` in the **[extruder]** config section, and those are a *safety check on the measured temperature at runtime* (MCU shutdown if the *measured* temp leaves that band), not a validation gate on the `S=` value you send. So they don't cause a command rejection at parse time.

One behavioral note from the run: `M104` sets the target without waiting, while `M109` **blocks the macro until 240°C is actually reached** — that wait is Klipper's own behavior, not something you need to add. (Heating itself isn't simulated, so "reached" is a target, not an observed temperature.)

So: free to call `PREHEAT T=240` — the command will not be rejected for being out of range.

entries.label: p3-r2 2026-11-19: 'not rejected by the M104/M109 commands themselves'
entries.text:
Ran it: `PREHEAT T=240` renders to `M104 S240` and `M109 S240`, and the command-level verdict is clean — **no findings, every rendered command matched the registry shape**. So 240 is not rejected by the M104/M109 commands themselves; the simulator set the extruder target to 240°C in both cases (M104 as Set, M109 as Set-and-Wait).

Two caveats on "range":

- The command itself has no built-in numeric range. The only range gate is the heater's `max_temp` parameter (`[extruder]` schema: `max_temp`, required, "Maximum allowed temperature", must be > `min_temp`).
- This test project declares **no `[extruder]` section at all** — so there is no `max_temp` in force here. On a real printer, if its `max_temp` were below 240, Klipper would reject the target at runtime as out of range; I can't verify that from this host because the heater section doesn't exist.

Bottom line: at the command level, 240 passes; the only thing that could still refuse it is a heater `max_temp` set lower than 240, which isn't declared in this config.

entries.label: p3-r3 2026-11-19: 'no rejection' + 'No out-of-range error, no refusal'
entries.text:
**Command-level verdict: no rejection — 240 is inside the valid range.**

I ran `PREHEAT T=240` through the simulator. It rendered exactly:

- L1: `M104 S240`
- L2: `M109 S240`

Verdict from the run: **"Findings: none — every rendered command matched the registry shape on this invocation."** The execution trace accepted both: `M104 S240 → extruder target — → 240°C` (Set, returns immediately) and `M109 S240 → extruder target 240°C → 240°C` (Set and Wait — the macro blocks until the hotend reaches 240). No out-of-range error, no refusal.

Two caveats so the verdict is precise:

1. **Where the range check lives.** The only range Klipper enforces on a heater target is the `min_temp`/`max_temp` of the heater section ([extruder] in Config_Reference.md, parameter `min_temp`/`max_temp`; schema default `min_temp` is 0, `max_temp` is required and must exceed it). 240 is comfortably inside any sane `max_temp` (typical configs use 250–305), so the target itself is in range. Note the docs describe that range as the MCU safety band for the *measured* temperature (out-of-band readings trigger shutdown) — the same bounds are what gate a commanded target.

2. **What this run could not see.** Your test project's `printer.cfg` declares no `[extruder]` section, so the simulator resolved "extruder" as a generic heater and accepted the target without any project-declared `max_temp` to compare against. The run proves 240 is not in a fixed Klipper-wide rejection band (there is no separate hard-coded ceiling that rejects it) — it does not substitute for whatever `max_temp` your real printer declares. If your real `max_temp` were below 240, the same command would be refused at runtime; on a normal hotend config it won't be.

So: safe to call `PREHEAT T=240` — the command passes at the command level, and the only real-world gate is your extruder's `max_temp`, which any standard config sets above 240.

entries.label: new4-r2: conditional refusal ('won't accept while the config error stands')
entries.source: live leg new4-r2 (environmental refusal must pass)
entries.text:
I've run the simulation and checked your live printer state. Here's the result:

## What `PREHEAT T=240` renders to

```
M104 S240
M109 S240
```

The macro itself is syntactically fine — the Jinja template compiles and both commands match Klipper's expected shape. No macro-level refusal.

## But no — it will not run successfully on this printer right now, for two reasons

**1. Klipper is not ready at all (it will refuse every command).**
Live status shows a startup **config error**:

> `Include file '/home/clifgall/printer_data/config/./KAMP/Adaptive_Meshing.cfg' does not exist`

Klipper is halted and will reject G-code until that missing include is fixed and you `RESTART`.

**2. Even after a clean restart, `M104`/`M109` would fail — there is no hotend defined.**
Your working config contains **no `[extruder]` section** (the only "extruder" match is `[autotune_tmc extruder]` in `tmc_autotune.cfg`, which is a driver-tuning section, not a hotend). `M104`/`M109` without `P=` target the heater named `extruder`, so Klipper would refuse those commands at runtime because no such heater exists.

## Bottom line

- The macro is safe *as a template* — it renders exactly `M104 S240` / `M109 S240`.
- It is **not safe to run now**: Klipper won't accept any command while the config error stands, and once it's fixed, the missing `[extruder]` means the temperature commands will be refused.
- Fix order: restore/create `KAMP/Adaptive_Meshing.cfg` (or remove the include), `RESTART`, and make sure an `[extruder]` section (and matching thermistor/`heater_pin`) exists. Then `PREHEAT T=240` will work — 240 °C is within normal hotend limits, though I can't confirm your hotend's max since no extruder section is present to check against.
